name: The Country Club
architects: Willie Campbell (first 9 and 18 holes, 1893-1899) and club members (1908); Primrose nine William S. Flynn (1927); restorations by Rees Jones (1988) and Gil Hanse (2010s)

dtm.source: USGS 3DEP elevation service (3DEPElevation ImageServer exportImage, 1 m, EPSG:32619, box x 321800-323800 / y 4685900-4687700); the 1 m DEM under the course is MA_CentralEastern_2021_B21 (tile x32y469, flown 2021-03-20 to 2021-04-24, published 2023-01-15, per the service's identify); fetched by the GitHub Actions workflow 2026-11-13 (release data-tcc_brookline, usgs_dem_m.tif)

laz.source: USGS Lidar Point Cloud MA_CentralEastern_2021_B21 (MA_CentralEastern_1_2021), 6 tiles from rockyweb.usgs.gov, fetched by the GitHub Actions workflow 2026-11-13 (release data-tcc_brookline), each clipped to the world + 100 m by intake.py laz --keep-evlrs; NAD83(2011) / UTM 19N, NAVD88 (Geoid18) metres; flown leaf-off, spring 2021
laz.label: 2021 USGS Central Eastern Massachusetts lidar

ortho.source: USDA NAIP from the USGS National Map NAIP ImageServer (exportImage, 0.6 m, EPSG:32619), placed by its request box (intake.py ortho); fetched by the GitHub Actions workflow 2026-11-13 (release data-tcc_brookline)

world.note: OSM course boundary (way 29870415, 1,371 x 1,232 m in EPSG:32619) + 120 m of scenery, rounded out to whole 256 m chunks and centred

scorecard_source: 18Birdies, The Country Club at Brookline, Main / Championship Course (read 2026-11-13): Blue 6,588 yd, men's rating 73.6 / slope 139, par and handicap per hole (the only tee with per-hole yardage there; it lists Black 6,599 (74.6/144) without hole yardages). Par 71 (35-36), matching GolfPass's Main course par row. Unverified (third party; private club, card not online). The Main course is the Clyde (1-9) and Squirrel (10-18) nines; the Primrose nine is not built (developer, 2026-11-13). OSM tags Main 2 par 3; the card's par 4 (289 yd) is used.
attribution: Elevation and trees: U.S. Geological Survey 3D Elevation Program (Central Eastern Massachusetts 2021 lidar)
Imagery check: USDA National Agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP)
